instructions: Place {left_cube} just to the left of {reference} and {right_cube} just to its right, both on the table. Judge left and right from in front of the robot.
Flank {reference} with the other two cubes: {left_cube} on its left and {right_cube} on its right. All three should rest on the table; use the view from in front of the robot.
Put {left_cube} beside the left side of {reference}, then put {right_cube} beside its right side. Left and right are as seen from in front of the robot.
The desired arrangement has {reference} between {left_cube} on the left and {right_cube} on the right, with both neighbours close by on the table. Use the view from in front of the robot.
Give {reference} a close neighbour on each side: {left_cube} to the left and {right_cube} to the right, resting on the table. Judge sides while facing the robot from the front.
Arrange the cubes on the table so that {left_cube} sits immediately left of {reference} and {right_cube} sits immediately right of it. Left and right use the view from in front of the robot.
notes: Introduces two independently assigned movable neighbours on opposite sides of one reference instead of positioning one object between two landmarks.
